section_summary: This section covers Japanese communist activity, labor disputes, and the perceived revival of ultra-rightist groups in late 1948. It contains a Tokyo despatch with two translated press articles, followed by duplicate file copies of those documents, airgrams about union leader Dobashi Kazuyoshi, and the opening pages of a March 1949 review of communism in Japan.

subfiles.title: Tokyo Despatch No. 716, concluding pages
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Assesses communist activity in Hokkaido and Kyushu and Japanese concern about nearby Soviet and communist power.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages compare communist organization in Hokkaido and Kyushu, including labor agitation and alleged Soviet or continental contacts. They argue that Soviet control near Hokkaido and developments in Korea and Manchuria have made communism a more immediate concern to Japanese observers.

subfiles.title: Attorney General's transmittal of FBI memorandum
subfiles.to: George C. Marshall, Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Forwards an FBI memorandum on the Research Institute of International Problems.
subfiles.summary: Forwards an FBI memorandum dated November 10 and its enclosure.

subfiles.title: Japanese Concern Over Communist-Rightist Conflict, Despatch No. 760
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits two translated press articles and assesses communist and ultra-rightist activity in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The despatch summarizes articles about communist organization in the Toho strike and emerging anti-communist rightist groups. It judges the ultra-rightist movement limited but potentially dangerous, especially if confrontation with communists grows amid economic instability. It also suggests that leftist publicity about fascist revival may partly divert attention from pressure on communists.

subfiles.title: Fractional Activities of Revolutionists
subfiles.about: Alleges that communist fractions manipulated labor organizations and prolonged the Toho studio strike.
subfiles.summary: The article argues that small communist groups could disrupt transport, communications, policing, and industry. Its main case is the Toho strike, where it alleges coordinated union support, manipulation of mediation, intimidation, and preparations for wider revolutionary action. These are the article's claims rather than independently established findings.

subfiles.title: Rising Rightists to Bait the Communists
subfiles.about: Surveys postwar Japanese anti-communist organizations and alleged political violence.
subfiles.summary: Yamamoto traces rightist activity from wartime groups to postwar anti-communist leagues, describing their leaders, membership, aims, and regional networks. He discusses alleged assassination attempts against communist leaders and urges opposition to terrorist factions while allowing lawful anti-communist activity.

subfiles.title: Routing memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 760
subfiles.about: Highlights Sebald's assessment and recommends circulation of the despatch.
subfiles.summary: Summarizes the despatch and recommends reading and routing it for reproduction.

subfiles.title: File copy of Japanese Concern Over Communist-Rightist Conflict
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Duplicates the assessment and transmittal in Despatch No. 760.
subfiles.summary: A poorly reproduced file copy of pages 182–188, covering communist and ultra-rightist activity and the possible consequences of conflict between them.

subfiles.title: File copy of Fractional Activities of Revolutionists
subfiles.about: Duplicates the article alleging communist manipulation of labor organizations and the Toho strike.
subfiles.summary: A poorly reproduced copy of the first article enclosed with Despatch No. 760. It presents allegations about communist fractions and the Toho studio strike.

subfiles.title: File copy of Rising Rightists to Bait the Communists
subfiles.about: Duplicates Yamamoto's survey of postwar anti-communist organizations.
subfiles.summary: A poorly reproduced copy of the second article enclosed with Despatch No. 760. It discusses rightist groups and alleged terrorist plots.

subfiles.title: Airgram on Dobashi Kazuyoshi joining the Japan Communist Party
subfiles.about: Reports Dobashi's formal Communist Party membership and planned Diet candidacy.
subfiles.summary: Reports that labor leader Dobashi Kazuyoshi formally joined the Communist Party and intended to stand for the Diet in Tokyo. It links him to the Communication Workers Union and opposition to revision of the National Public Service Law.

subfiles.title: Correction to airgram on Dobashi Kazuyoshi
subfiles.about: Corrects the earlier account of Dobashi's union offices.
subfiles.summary: Corrects the claim that Dobashi chaired the National Congress of Industrial Unions.

subfiles.title: Communism in Japan
subfiles.about: Proposes periodic summaries and analysis of communist activities in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Proposes a recurring analytical summary using diplomatic reporting on Japanese communism.

subfiles.title: A Review of Communism in Japan
subfiles.from: Willis Lory, Division of Northeast Asian Affairs
subfiles.about: Begins a historical and thematic review of Japanese communism from 1921 through the postwar period.
subfiles.summary: The title page and contents introduce a report covering party history and communist activities in labor, youth, farming, women's groups, the press, theater, and education. The surviving opening pages recount the party's founding, repression, Comintern connections, Nosaka's wartime activity in China, and its postwar revival. The section ends during an account of Communist efforts to establish a popular front after 1945.
